jobs.title: Growth Product Manager (Senior to Staff)
jobs.description:
At DistroKid, we help artists share their music with the world. Around 40-50% of the world's new music is released through DistroKid today.

We're hiring a Growth Product Manager (Senior to Staff level) to help us achieve our big vision that everyone who makes music has a DistroKid account.

At DistroKid, our product and marketing funnels evolved in parallel. This role unites them and owns the whole picture: member growth end to end, from how artists find us through to how they get value and stay for the long haul. Within the goals leadership sets, you’ll establish where the leverage is, back it with data, and ship.

We're looking for someone who has done this before. You've owned growth at a high-growth consumer or subscription business, you've seen what works and what doesn't across the funnel, and you'll arrive with a point of view on what we should do. A big part of this role is bringing that experience with you and helping the rest of the company get better at growth.

You'll partner with our staff marketing engineer to direct a small, diligent cross-functional team, and work with them while working across product, marketing, data, and design. This role reports into product and treats marketing as an equal partner in setting priorities. You'll shape a single growth backlog, balancing measurable wins against the longer-term bets worth protecting. You'll build the framework that sizes every growth opportunity on the same terms, so prioritization performs on evidence and expected impact. Ideas and market intelligence come from across the company; you turn the greatest of them into instrumented experiments tied to the product roadmap.

What You’ll Do:

  • Own member growth, the growth strategy, and the prioritized backlog that moves it, and build the measurement framework the company uses to size and evaluate growth bets
  • Navigate the full funnel to achieve our growth goals, including acquisition, onboarding, activation, retention, reactivation, and referrals
  • Set the standard for how we run experiments end to end: hypothesis, instrumentation, analysis, iteration, and knowing when to stop
  • Use AI tooling to compress the loop from idea to shipped experiment, multiplying what a small, nimble team can ship
  • Keep the executive team clear on what you're doing, why, and what you're trading off
  • Bring what you've learned on the consumer growth teams you've worked on (and keep learning from the best ones), and adapt it to how artists find and use DistroKid
  • Raise the growth bar across the company, helping PMs and marketers surface and clear their own growth blockers
  • Use and iterate on the artist tools and promo assets we already have to build organic and viral growth loops.

What We're Looking For:

  • 7+ years in product, including 5+ years working directly in growth
  • 3+ years owning a growth number (paying members, conversion, retention, or self-serve revenue) and the metrics that drive it, at a high-growth consumer or subscription business
  • Experience across several parts of the funnel (acquisition, conversion, activation, engagement, retention and churn), not just one step
  • You’ve set growth strategy yourself. You found the opportunities, made the calls, and can point to the numbers that moved because of it
  • You conduct experiments at scale, pull your own data, and know the difference between a real result and noise
  • You've used AI tools to get real growth or productivity gains, not just experimented with them
  • You take rough, half-formed ideas from across the company and turn them into plans a team is excited to perform
  • You’ve seen enough consumer and subscription growth to arrive with informed views on where the opportunity is, and you change them when the data tells you to
  • You make complicated things simple and explain them well, including the trade-offs
  • It's a bonus (but not required) to have:
    • familiarity with lifecycle and martech tooling
    • experience designing and enhancing personalized surfaces (and a clear sense of when personalization earns its complexity and when it doesn't)

What You’ll Work With

  • A dedicated growth team including engineering, data, and design support
  • A reporting line into our Chief Product Officer, and marketing as a co-owner of the growth backlog
  • High traffic volume and a product millions of artists already love
  • A company that values speed, creativity, and clear thinking

jobs.title: Lead Product Manager
jobs.description:
Every team has AI. Few have mastered it. Humans were built to adapt, but AI is now moving faster than most workforces can.
 Multiverse is the AI adoption layer: the missing link between the AI tools that companies have invested in and the people expected to use them.

jobs.title: Technical Product Manager - Developer Experience (DevEx)
jobs.description:
Our mission

 We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

 In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.

 We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

 Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

 How you'll help us achieve it 

 Your mission is to make it dramatically easier for our engineers to ship features and learn from them quickly, securely, and reliably. You'll aim for small-startup speed while meeting the quality bar of a large financial institution. Velocity here means removing friction and toil from the path between idea and learning, not asking people to work harder.

 AI is a big part of the opportunity, and we're looking for a PM who is optimistic about its possibilities but pragmatic about what actually works. The goal is not to adopt the latest shiny AI tool; it's to deeply understand your internal users, experiment, and honestly evaluate what solves their problems, whether that's AI, process changes, or boring tooling that just works.

 The Technical Product Manager - DevEx will:

 
 Lead a team of engineers with full ownership of how we deliver new features for our users and use AI solutions to remove impactful friction for our engineers and product managers.

 Define product goals, metrics, and roadmaps based on user needs and mission impact.

 Drive user research within our engineering and product teams.

 Write clear, compelling design docs and facilitate async, fast-moving decision-making.

 Over-communicate context, priorities, and decisions to ensure team alignment.

 Adjust priorities quickly based on feedback, experiments, or new learnings.

 Solve problems holistically, whether through product features, ops tooling or process changes.

 
 In this role, you'll... 

 
 Own the developer experience holistically, including any internal or external tooling needed to support it.

 Research and implement solutions for how we can use AI to remove engineering and development friction. 

 Build your own prototypes to test ideas where possible.

 Relentlessly gather feedback (by talking to users and looking at data) to deeply understand the problem space and our engineers' and product managers' needs.

 Work from first principles to understand the engineers' and product managers' biggest problems and then figure out how our tooling should work to solve those problems.

 Prioritize the biggest problems blocking the engineers' and product managers' productivity and the impact on delivering value to our users fast and securely.

 Directly manage the DevEx team to help them grow in their careers, partnering with the Tech Lead, who will own the technical bar.

 
 Key Details 

 
 This is a fully remote role. Candidates must be based in one of our talent hub countries (UK, Spain, USA (East Coast), Canada, Kenya and Ghana) or in one of our operating markets in Africa including Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, or Burkina Faso

 Wave is a distributed team, and we fund up to three in-person get-togethers a year, in line with Wave's travel policy.

 Our salaries are competitive and are calculated using a transparent formula. For this role, depending on your level and location, we offer a salary up to $237,500 USD, plus a generous equity package.

 Major benefits:

 
 Subsidized health insurance for you and your dependents, and retirement contributions (both vary from country to country).

 6 months of fully paid parental leave and subsidized fertility assistance.

 Flexible vacation, with most folks taking between 21-30 days per year. 

 $10,000 annual charitable donation matching.

 Have 3+ years of product management experience and hands-on engineering background (you've shipped production code) or direct PM ownership of a developer experience, or developer productivity function.

 Proven success in overseeing all elements of the product development lifecycle, such as user research, design, implementation and evaluation.

 Speak fluent English

 Have professional experience in a consumer fintech company

jobs.description:
Product Manager, Device Data Management (Français/Anglais) 
 Lieu : Paris, France (hybride, trois jours par semaine au bureau)
 Niveau : Senior Product Manager
 Équipe : Device Data Management (DDM)
 Contrat : CDI
 À noter : ce poste est basé en France. Vous devez donc y résider ou être prêt·e à déménager, et disposer déjà du droit de travailler dans l’UE. Nous ne pouvons pas proposer de sponsoring de visa, mais nous l’examinons poste par poste : gardez un œil sur notre site carrières pour les opportunités à venir. 
 Un français et un anglais courants (à l’oral comme à l’écrit) sont indispensables, et nous vous demandons de soumettre votre CV en anglais . À propos de Kaluza 
 Kaluza est la plateforme d’Energy Intelligence qui transforme la complexité de l’énergie en coordination fluide. Nous aidons les acteurs de l’énergie à relever les défis d’aujourd’hui tout en accélérant la transition vers un avenir propre et électrifié.
 Notre plateforme orchestre des millions de décisions en temps réel à travers les foyers, les appareils, les marchés et les réseaux. En combinant algorithmes prédictifs et conception centrée sur l’humain, Kaluza rend l’énergie propre fiable, abordable et adaptée à la vie quotidienne.
 Avec des équipes en Europe, en Asie et en Australie, et une joint-venture avec Mitsubishi Corporation au Japon, nous accompagnons des acteurs majeurs comme OVO, AGL et ENGIE, ainsi que des innovateurs comme Volvo et Volkswagen.
 Ce que vous ferez : 
 Vous serez responsable de la localisation française de Device Data Management (DDM), l’un des domaines produit clés de la plateforme Kaluza. DDM consomme des flux de données internes et externes pour représenter les fournitures, compteurs, registres, relevés et consommations. Il gère aussi les parcours liés à ces entités (par exemple, la mise à jour de la configuration d’un compteur), les API qui exposent les données, les pages front-end qui les présentent aux utilisateurs, ainsi que les calculs de projection et d’extrapolation de consommation. C’est un rôle produit full-stack et très opérationnel : vous interviendrez sur tout le domaine, du modèle de données jusqu’à ce que voient les utilisateurs à l’écran.
 Traduire les exigences du marché français en spécifications claires : transformer les règles du marché de l’énergie français (Enedis, GRDF, passerelle GRD, règles sur les données de compteurs et d’équipements) en exigences produit détaillées couvrant la conformité réglementaire, les flux de données des équipements et la qualité des données.

 Travailler en étroite collaboration avec nos clients : collaborer main dans la main avec ENGIE et les futurs clients du marché français pour comprendre leurs besoins et construire les exigences ensemble. Bâtir une relation de confiance telle qu’ils viennent vous voir en premier, et vous appuyer sur cette proximité pour orienter ce que DDM construira ensuite pour la France.

 Construire, pas seulement spécifier : passer vous-même de l’idée au prototype fonctionnel en interrogeant les données, en esquissant des contrats d’API et en montant des preuves de concept. Nous attendons de vous que vous utilisiez quotidiennement des outils d’IA (ex. Claude Code) comme multiplicateur pour prototyper, investiguer et débloquer des situations, et pas seulement pour rédiger des documents.

 Aligner les équipes globales et locales, toutes fonctions confondues : travailler étroitement avec l’ingénierie, l’UX, la QA et bien d’autres, avec une influence full-stack, pour que tout le monde vise les bons résultats.

 Être la personne de référence pour DDM France : faire le lien entre nos équipes globales et locales afin d’éclairer les priorités et la stratégie.

 Ce que vous apportez : 
 Critères essentiels :
 Une expérience avérée en tant que Product Manager, Business Analyst ou équivalent dans des éditeurs de logiciels, avec un solide historique de localisation réussie de produits logiciels complexes pour des marchés internationaux

 Un français courant et une grande aisance en anglais : notre plateforme et beaucoup de nos équipes fonctionnent en anglais, vous passez donc facilement de l’un à l’autre

 De l’aisance dans le travail direct avec les clients : vous savez animer une session de travail avec des interlocuteurs clients, faire émerger le vrai besoin derrière la demande, et garder les décideurs alignés et impliqués

 Un état d’esprit de bâtisseur et une aisance technique : débrouillard·e et opérationnel·le, vous préférez construire un prototype fonctionnel plutôt qu’attendre la spécification parfaite. Vous êtes à l’aise avec les modèles de données, les bases de données et les API, et vous pouvez tenir une conversation technique. Vous n’avez pas besoin d’être ingénieur·e, mais vous raisonnez comme tel·le, et vous êtes aussi à l’aise pour réfléchir à un modèle de données que pour penser à ce que l’utilisateur voit à l’écran

 Une communication claire et incisive, capable de faire le tri dans le bruit et d’expliquer la complexité tec

jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.description:
Join BLP and help make the world’s business processes autonomous! 
 Our agentic platform helps finance and operations teams worldwide remove manual work from their core business processes, so work runs end-to-end with greater control and significant productivity gains. 
 Today, over 550 enterprise customers use BLP across 1,300+ deployed projects. In the processes we automate, customers achieve productivity improvements of 5 to 10 times. 
 To date, BLP remains majority employee-owned, with Goldman Sachs holding a minority stake as a growth investor. Our success is driven by deep expertise in technology and business processes, a superior product with strong product-market fit, reflected in an expanding customer base that includes Fortune 500 companies. 
 BLP is one of Switzerland's fastest-growing SaaS scale-ups; we are now entering our next phase of growth. From our headquarters on Zürich's Bahnhofstrasse, we're expanding globally, with a growing presence across Europe and North America. 
 Join us and help make autonomous operations the new standard. 
 
 
 The opportunity 
 Our engineering teams build a product that enterprises run their purchase-to-pay and order-to-cash processes on every day. Much of the product knowledge behind it sits with our founders and domain experts. As we grow, we are moving from a project-oriented model, where features come top-down and success is measured by output, to a product-oriented one: empowered teams that own problems end-to-end and are measured by their impact on customers and the business.
 As Head of Product, you lead that shift. You build the product management practice for the BLP Platform from an early stage. Our first product managers are joining stream-aligned teams, starting with Invoice and Procurement, and the team will grow to 4–5 PMs as we expand. You hire them, coach them, and set the standard for what great product work looks like at BLP.
 You report to the CTO and work closely with Engineering, Projects, Sales, and our founders.
 What you’ll do 
 Build and lead the product management practice for the BLP Platform: hire, coach, and develop a team of product managers as we scale.

 Move the product organization from an output-driven model to an outcome-driven one.

 Establish the product management craft at BLP: discovery practices, evidence-based decision making, and a clear standard for what “good” looks like in the role.

 Transfer product knowledge out of the experts’ heads and into the teams, without losing the domain depth that got us here.

 Build the direct line between our teams and our customers.

 Make our data usable for product decisions. We have BigQuery, PostHog, and prediction-rate analytics available, and we want product managers who reach for them by default.

 Shape how the product organization works as we grow: intake, prioritization, roadmapping, and the operating rhythm.

 Contribute directly to product strategy for the platform.

 What you bring 
 10+ years in product management, including experience leading or formally coaching product managers, with a real point of view on how product people are developed.

 Experience working in an empowered product model, where teams were assigned problems to solve rather than features to build.

 A track record of shipping enterprise B2B software that customers actually adopted.

 Experience moving an organization toward an empowered product model, including the political and cultural side of it.

 The ability to hold a position with engineers, sales, and executives, and to say no in a way that keeps the relationship.

 Entrepreneurial judgment: comfortable operating with incomplete information, choosing a direction, and owning the result.

 Fluent English.

 Enterprise ERP or finance exposure, experience with AI or agentic products in production (particularly reliability, evaluation, and trust in enterprise settings), and German are a plus.

 Why BLP 
 Build a function: you shape how product management works at BLP while the team grows.

 Direct work with the CTO and founders on product strategy for the platform.

 A product with deep domain substance and a large enterprise customer base to learn from.

 Employee participation plan.

 How we work 
 Impact: We create measurable business outcomes.

 Transparency: We build trust through openness.

 Ownership: We take responsibility for outcomes.

 Excellence: We relentlessly strive for greatness.

 Practical information 
 Location: hybrid from our Zurich, London, Munich or Cologne offices, or remote elsewhere in Europe.

 Employment: full-time, permanent.

jobs.title: Senior Growth Product Manager
jobs.description:
Data quality is the bottleneck of the AI era. Every Fortune 500 is trying to solve it. We're the team they call.
 Soda is the data quality layer for Disney, Ralph Lauren, CBRE, HelloFresh, 2K Games, and Nubank. Our open-source engine, Soda Core, is used by companies like Tesla, Slack, Adyen, Walmart, and JPMC. The category is growing fast because AI doesn't work on bad data, and we're hiring a Senior Growth Product Manager to get customers using Soda faster and on more of their data.
 About Us
 Soda's mission is to monitor the world's decisions. We're building the first Data & AI performance monitoring platform that spans data collection to automated decision-making. Soda helps customers find, understand, and fix data quality issues by combining automated post-production monitoring with pre-production pipeline data testing.
 Soda was founded in 2019 by Maarten (employee #5 at Collibra) and Tom (creator of multiple open-source projects generating hundreds of millions in value). We commercialize through Soda Cloud and we're well-funded, with investors like Point 9 Capital, Hummingbird, Singular, and Eurazeo.
 The Role
 You'll lead our adoption team, a small group of frontend, full-stack, and AI engineers. The team works on onboarding and activation, on keeping workflows coherent across the product, on customer-facing dashboards, and on AI features that save users work.
 Most of our roadmap is driven by what customers and prospects ask for. This team's work is driven by adoption metrics, because customers rarely ask for the things that would make them use Soda more. You'll start from a hypothesis, for example that changing a flow will get 20% more data contracts created, ship the change, and check whether it worked.
 We sell to enterprises, so sample sizes are small and A/B tests rarely reach significance. You'll use product analytics, session replays, and conversations with users, and you'll often have to decide with incomplete data. This is a product role. If most of your growth experience is in paid acquisition or lifecycle email, it's probably the wrong fit. You'll also work closely with our Growth team, which is led by a co-founder, on launches and messaging.
 What You'll Do
 Own the adoption metrics for Soda Cloud: time to first verified contract for new accounts, data coverage (datasets with contracts and monitors), weekly active datasets and users, and usage of AI features. You'll define them, make sure we can measure them, and improve them.
 Own the UX of workflows across the product and keep them coherent for our two kinds of users: data engineers, and business users such as data stewards and governance leads.
 Find where customers get stuck between signing the contract and running Soda on most of their data, and decide what to fix first.
 Design and ship onboarding flows that get a new team to first value within days, including self-serve paths for technical teams that want to evaluate Soda on their own.
 Put AI to work on adoption: decide which steps an agent should do for the user, ship them with the team, and measure whether people keep using them.
 Work with Growth on launches and product marketing, and with our customer engineers on whatever is blocking rollouts at customers.
 Hiring Process
 Application: your CV, plus a short answer about one metric you moved (what it was, what you shipped, what happened, and what didn't work)
 15-minute phone screen
 First interview (60 min): a deep dive into product growth work you've done. Part of it is showing us something you shipped that you'd still be proud to demo.
 Second interview (60 min): a working session on a real Soda adoption problem
 Culture fit (45 min)
 We answer every application, and every candidate hears back within 3–5 days of each step. If it's not a hell yes, it's a no, and we'll tell you quickly and kindly.
 Requirements 
 You Should Have
 5+ years in product, including at least 2 owning growth, activation, onboarding, or adoption in B2B SaaS : you were accountable for a metric for long enough to see whether your changes worked. In your application, tell us which metric it was, where it started and where it ended, what you shipped, and what didn't work.
 Product craft and taste : you love software and have used a lot of it yourself, so you know what a good product feels like. You keep scope small, work in short cycles with engineers and designers, run your own customer calls, and have well-reasoned opinions about UX.
 An AI-native way of working and building : you've shipped an AI-powered feature and measured whether people use it, you prototype with coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.), and you're happy to open a small PR yourself for something like a copy change.
 You do your own analysis : you write SQL, build funnels yourself, and know when a sample is too small to conclude anything.
 Experience with technical products : you've built for engineers or data teams and are comfortable talking about pipelines, warehouses, and APIs.

jobs.title: Product Support & Enablement Lead
jobs.description:
About Mistral 
 Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.
 We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.
 
 About the role 
 We are looking for a Product Support & Enablement Lead to lead and develop our existing L1 Product Support team. You will help the team resolve more customer issues without escalating to L2, while improving the tools, training, and workflows that allow support to scale.
 This is a senior technical and people-management role—not simply a role overseeing today’s queue. You will lead frontline delivery for Product Support (L1) and develop the team’s ability to investigate and resolve increasingly technical requests, including paid self-serve and first-level enterprise issues.
 You will work closely with L2 and other teams to define clear ownership, identify work Product Support (L1) can safely take on, and build repeatable escalation paths. You will also contribute to operational continuity for the wider Support organization.

 Lead frontline support delivery 
 Lead, coach, and develop a distributed L1 Product Support team, providing regular feedback and supporting technical growth.

 Define and maintain clear ownership of L1 Product Support queues and handoffs to L2, including for paid self-serve and first-level enterprise requests.

 Monitor service quality, response and resolution times, backlog health, and customer satisfaction; turn insights into practical improvements.

 Stay hands-on with complex or sensitive customer issues and model strong technical judgment.

 Improve L1-to-L2 handoffs so escalations contain customer impact, investigation steps, and relevant evidence.

 Track escalation patterns and use them to prioritize training, documentation, and product improvements.

 Own improvements to frontline Product Support (L1) tooling, routing, workflows, macros, and internal processes.

 Develop AI-assisted support and automation, including Intercom Fin, to reduce repetitive work while maintaining response quality and appropriate human escalation.

 Identify recurring contact drivers and partner with Product, Engineering, and other teams to address them at the source.

 Build reporting and operating reviews that make workload, service performance, escalation patterns, and risks visible.

 Establish shared processes with specialist Support teams while respecting their ownership of technical delivery.

 Build knowledge and operational continuity 
 Develop onboarding materials and technical training that help agents become autonomous.

 Work with Documentation and Product teams to keep internal guidance and customer-facing help content accurate and useful.

 Share customer insights and support trends with Product, Engineering, and go-to-market teams.

 Help coordinate support readiness for new products, features, and processes.

 Contribute to operational continuity for the Support organization through team coordination, reporting, and escalation management.
